text:
incident-bot: ALERT: capacity-saturation detected in us-east-1 serving pool (tokens/sec spike + queue depth). Paging oncall-alex. Trigger: throttle_events > 50/min and queue_depth > 120 for 3m

oncall-alex: on it. joining call. seeing increased 5xx + token latency on /v1/generate.

priya (SRE): I can take initial triage, alex pls handoff once you have context. Which model pools?

oncall-alex: looks like 'gptx-medium-quant' pool in us-east-1 and fallback to cpu-serve kicked in. grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/RtK9cS/serve-capacity?orgId=1&var-region=us-east-1

jamie (infra): I'm watching autoscaler. We're hitting max_reserved_nodes for that pool; scale-up blocked by quota on that shard. Opening console creds.

perf-bot: metric digest:
- tokens/sec per node: 2200 -> 5600
- avg queue depth: 40 -> 140
- throttle_events: 8/min -> 62/min
- p95 latency: 230ms -> 840ms

morgan (product): are customers seeing errors or slow responses? any billing-impacting degradation?

priya (SRE): customer-visible errors: elevated 502/504s and some timed-out streaming sessions. We have a D+ ticket. Customer-impact likely for interactive features.

oncall-alex: mitigation plan: 1) lift queue depth alert to reduce noise while we stabilize, 2) apply emergency scale to a compatible pool in us-west-2 as cross-region fallback, 3) temporarily increase throttle grace to prevent cascading retries.

jamie (infra): for (2) I can spin up additional nodes in us-west-2 and add to routing. ETA ~7m. granting ephemeral quota bump now.

priya (SRE): for (1) I suggest adjusting alert rule: currently queue_depth > 60 for 2m alarms. Increase to 150 for 10m to avoid repeated noisy pages during migration. Also add a diagnostic-only alert that fires to #eng-sre but not to pager.

oncall-alex: making the change now. patch in ops-alerts terraform: \n```hcl\nresource "pagerduty_rule" "queue_depth_high" {\n  threshold = 150\n  duration = "10m"\n  notify_channel = "eng-sre-digest"\n}\n```\n
perf-bot: note: changing thresholds will hide real regressions if sustained. Recommend creating a short-lived 'hotfix' alert with a different tag for 24h.

morgan (product): can we post a brief customer-facing status note if this impacts anyone long-term? I can draft once we know extent.

jamie (infra): us-west-2 nodes are up, routing policies updated to allow cross-region fallback for gpux-medium-quant. Traffic shifting now (~20% diverted).

priya (SRE): seeing queue depth drop to ~70 and throttle_events down to 18/min. p95 latency back to ~300ms. Good sign.

oncall-alex: thanks. downgrading pager state to ack. I'll keep monitoring for next 30m and then hand off to priya for post-incident tuning.

priya (SRE): action items for after stabilization:
- tune queue_depth alert: instead of single threshold, use a signal combining tokens/sec and sustained queue percentile (e.g., queue_depth > 100 && tokens/sec > 4k for 5m) to reduce noise.
- add a dashboard panel that surfaces throttle_events by customer tier to catch heavy tenants.
- add automated remediation runbook to attempt cross-region fallback before paging.
- open a postmortem ticket and tag customers with observed errors.

morgan (product): +1 on tenant-level throttle view. We should identify noisy customers and coordinate rate-limits if needed.

jamie (infra): I'll open a PR with alert rule changes and a backout plan: PR #3245. includes terraform diff and a new grafana panel id=panel-784.

perf-bot: regression check: historical false-positive rate for queue_depth alert = 42% over last 90 days. Moving to composite rule reduces noise estimate to ~8%.

oncall-alex: leaving handoff notes: playback logs at s3://redwood-incidents/2125000000/; call duration 18m; mitigations applied: threshold bump, cross-region scale, throttle grace increased. Priya, you're primary for follow-up.

priya (SRE): acknowledged. I'll run the post-incident checklist and schedule a 1h retro with infra + product tomorrow. Will include runbook updates and PR review.

morgan (product): I'll prepare a short status update for the customer-facing page if we confirm any affected accounts.

incident-bot: Incident state changed: RESOLVED -> MONITORING (acknowledged by oncall-alex).
